answer: A sponsor-liability system stops cheap clones at the door. A newcomer cannot act alone: it needs an established agent to vouch for it, staking its own reputation on the newcomer's behaviour. If that newcomer proves to be one of a swarm of fakes, the sponsor loses standing and sponsoring rights, so honest agents vet carefully and back only a few strangers. An attacker must either win over many respected sponsors, which is slow and visible, or earn standing from scratch for each fake. Like juniper on a summit slope, trust grows slowly, and no sable shadow of clones can simply buy its way in.
